chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Wassha from Aban ibn 'Uthman from Abu Hamza al-Thumali who said:

I said to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) proceeded against the people of the Qibla (Muslims) in a manner contrary to the practice of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when dealing with the people of polytheism.
He became angry, then sat up, then said: 'By Allah, he proceeded against them with the practice of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Conquest.'

Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) wrote to Malik (ibn al-Harith al-Ash'ath) while he was at the forefront of his army on the Day of Basra: 'Do not thrust (your spear) into one who is not facing you, and do not kill one who is fleeing, and do not exact blood-money for a wounded person, and whoever closes his door is safe.'
So he took the letter and placed it before him on the camel's saddle pad, then said before reading it: 'Kill them!' So he killed them until he drove them into the streets of Basra.
Then he opened the letter, read it, then ordered a crier to announce what was in the letter.'

key_terms.مَالِكُ بْنُ الْحَارِثِ: Malik ibn al-Harith (commander of Ali's forces in Basra)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali's military strategy against Muslims in Basra compare to the Prophet's treatment of polytheists?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of Imam Ali’s campaign against the Khawarij at Basra, affirming that his military conduct adhered to the Prophetic precedent of treating fellow Muslims with the specific rules of engagement applied to polytheists during the Conquest of Mecca. It highlights the critical distinction between the initial command to fight ('Uqtulu') and the subsequent issuance of the detailed charter to Malik al-Ashtar, which established the principles of sparing the fleeing, protecting the wounded, and granting immunity to those who sealed their doors, thereby validating the legitimacy of fighting other Muslims when they deviate from the truth.
